title: IMPact De-implementation of Proven Ineffective Nursing Routines
summary:
Hospitals have many nursing activities that have been carried out routinely for many years. Some have become a normal part of everyday care. However, research shows that some of these routines do not benefit patients. They may still be continued even when there is no good reason to do so. This can take up nursing time, use resources, and place unnecessary burden on patients.
The WIRKUNG project aims to identify nursing routines that have been proven to be ineffective and to stop them safely. This should create more time for nursing care that truly benefits patients.
Nurses from all inpatient areas of the university hospital can suggest routines that they believe should be reviewed. A team of professionals from different disciplines will carefully assess these suggestions. The most suitable routines will then be examined using current scientific evidence. A routine will only be considered for removal if there is sufficient evidence that it provides no benefit.
Selected routines will first be stopped on suitable pilot wards. Staff will receive information, training, and support during the change. The effects will be monitored for six months, including nursing time, use of resources, and patient safety.
If the change works well and is safe, it can be introduced on other wards. The long-term goal is to create more time for effective nursing care and for patients.
